title: Polarization reduces coalitional influence
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^n$ to $\{-1,1\}$, let $(i_1,\ldots,i_m)$ be a finite list of coordinates, and let $J$ be a set of coordinates. The coalitional influence of the function obtained by successively polarizing $f$ in the listed coordinates is at most the coalitional influence of $f$ on $J$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
the polarization sequence is a finite list of coordinates
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates
